free_tier.stated: Free edition: permanently free, 1 Mbps, random URL subdomain, random TCP port, HTTP / TCP tunnel support, 1 online cpolar process, 4 tunnels per process. [translated]

egress.terms: No byte quota on any plan: every plan is sold with traffic not limited. The free plan's 1 Mbps caps a saturated month at about 324 GB.; ingress: tcp

interface_detail: Web UI on localhost:9200 after install, a CLI with authtoken authentication, and a dashboard at dashboard.cpolar.com.
tooling: vendor client on Windows/Linux/NAS/ARM, authenticating with a token from the dashboard; wg-quick cannot attach to it
chaining: Carries HTTP and TCP only, so it composes with a web service or an SSH control channel and not with WireGuard.

limits.value: connection-rate limit per tunnel endpoint; excess HTTP connections get 429, excess TCP connections are closed
1 online process and 4 tunnels on the free plan

binding_note: Traffic is unlimited but 1 Mbps is 10.5 GB/day, about 324 GB over 30 days, against 3.24 Mbps for 1 TiB/month. The shaping binds three times.

identity_cost.detail: An account is an email address: the pricing FAQ defines one online process as one email account installing a user on one machine, and says multiple machines means registering multiple email accounts.

reliability_note: Exceeding the connection rate limit returns 429 on HTTP and silently closes TCP and TLS connections; the vendor documents neither the threshold nor a reset window.
confidence_note: Pricing table read first-party and the whole documentation site searched for UDP with zero hits. A negative search is strong evidence here because the same docs page documents TCP, HTTP and TLS tunnels by name.

evidence.proved: free plan is 1 Mbps, random subdomain, random TCP port, HTTP/TCP tunnels only, 1 process, 4 tunnels; all plans state traffic is not limited
86941-byte documentation read contains no occurrence of UDP

notes: The best-identified Chinese tunnel vendor in English lists, with an email-only account, and the only one here with a documentation set large enough to make the absence of UDP meaningful. No English pricing arm was found: www.cpolar.com/en/pricing returns 404 and the only pricing page is the Chinese one.

extras.wg_detail: No UDP reconstruction exists: the pricing page lists only HTTP and TCP tunnels, and an 87 KB full-text read of the documentation site at /docs contains no occurrence of UDP at all.
extras.volume_stated: No byte quota on any plan: every plan is sold with traffic not limited. The free plan's 1 Mbps caps a saturated month at about 324 GB.
extras.transit_note: Vendor relays in mainland China carry the tunnel.
